newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bonds push NZ dollar weaker despite PM's comment.
newsitem.headline: Bonds push NZ dollar weaker despite PM's comment.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed sharply weaker on Thursday despite Prime Minister Jim Bolger's comment that a strong economy would inevitably mean a strong currency.

Dealers said the early Bolger comment gave some traders a brief excuse to bid the currency up, but they could not match an overhang of long positions and then a weakly-supported bond auction in the midsession compounded to the selling pressure.
"There were quite a few people caught long last night who sold out this morning," said one.
"It's been under pressure all day, basically," said another, who noted that the weaker Australian unit had not helped.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6930/37 and at 68.15 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6962/69 and 68.39 at the open.

The currency rallied slightly when Bolger said New Zealand was attempting to secure greater international competitiveness "while acknowledging that confidence in New Zealand's government and its economy will inevitably ensure a strong dollar". But it soon resumed its downward spiral.
"He's kind of stating the obvious, isn't he," said one trader, reflecting on the Bolger comment.
"I think the market certainly was long and was very relieved to see that comment come up, but I myself put more emphasis on what the Treasurer says or the governor of the Reserve Bank."
Poor demand in the NZ$50 million government tender of February 2016 inflation-indexed bonds was seen to confirm fragile tone in New Zealand debt securities at present.
"The bond auction didn't go well today and the Kiwi got sold on the back of that," said a dealer.
However, the New Zealand unit closed off its day lows, after finding solid support around 0.6920, and dealers saw it remaining in its broad 0.6920-80 range for the time being.
One put Thursday's 30 points sell-off in context, "If you look at the movement we've seen in dollar/yen in the last four or five trading days, the Kiwi's movement overnight and today is very small."
The Kiwi was expected to trade a 0.6925-65 range overnight.
